title: Single-Agent LLMs Outperform Multi-Agent Systems on Multi-Hop Reasoning Under Equal Thinking Token Budgets
venue: arXiv:2604.02460v2 (11 Apr 2026), preprint under review; Stanford

selection.evidence: Cited by lee2026-rhi (related work) for the claim that multi-agent gains can reflect extra compute. Chosen because it tests the premise of MASS ('multi-agent topologies excel at complex reasoning') under a matched budget.

cost.compute_notes: 27-page PDF: body and Appendix A-B read, Tables 3-10 parsed by script. No code released. t01 and t02 each run under 10 s.

triggers: single agent vs multi-agent equal budget

claims.statement: Under matched thinking-token budgets, a single agent is the best system or statistically indistinguishable from the best in every cell except the 100-token budget, across Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B, Gemini 2.5 Flash and Pro on FRAMES and MuSiQue 4-hop.
claims.scope: Short-answer multi-hop QA, LLM-judged correctness, budgets of 100-10k thinking tokens, five MAS designs (sequential, subtask-parallel, parallel roles, debate, ensemble).

quantities.name: cells_MA_sig_better_question_level
quantities.unit: cells (Gemini-2.5-Pro FRAMES at 500: SA 0.600 vs MA 0.660, z = -2.53)

our_assessment.why: With question-level SEs, 38 of 40 cells show no detectable difference. Single-agent is better in one (DeepSeek MuSiQue 1k, part of a consistent DeepSeek-MuSiQue pattern at every budget), and multi-agent is better in one, which the paper's blanket sentence contradicts. Supported: 'single agent MATCHES multi-agent at equal thinking tokens' for short-answer multi-hop QA. The title's 'outperform' holds only for DeepSeek on MuSiQue and against the Sequential design specifically. Scope is far from long-horizon coding or research, where MASS and RHI live: there the context-degradation exception the paper itself derives (c3) is the expected regime.

claims.statement: The appendix 95% bootstrap CIs (Tables 3-10, 168 cells) are 2-4x narrower than the binomial width at the question count, and they are not centred on their own point estimates. FRAMES widths imply n = 3,255 (median; FRAMES has 824 questions), MuSiQue widths imply n = 6,073. Point estimates sit in the outer 10% of their interval in 15% (FRAMES) and 10% (MuSiQue) of cells, and 2 lie outside it.

our_assessment.why: Our percentile bootstrap at n = 824 recovers n = 827 and a centred position of 0.50, so the check is calibrated. The FRAMES implied n is about 4 x 824, consistent with pooling repeated runs as if they were independent questions, with point estimates from a different sample. This is a hypothesis; the paper does not describe its bootstrap. Direction of the consequence: correct intervals would be wider, so MORE systems would be 'indistinguishable from the best'. That strengthens 'matches' and weakens 'outperforms'.

claims.statement: By the data processing inequality, a single agent with perfect use of the full context can do no worse than a multi-agent system that passes messages derived from that context. Multi-agent systems become competitive when single-agent context use degrades, or when they get extra compute.

our_assessment.why: The bound is correct and the paper states its own key assumption: perfect context utilisation. It is a statement about an ideal reader. Every long-horizon agent task (MASS, RHI) violates that assumption by design, so the theorem does not bear on them, and the authors say as much.

claims.statement: API budget control is unreliable: Gemini 2.5's visible thinking plateaus well below the requested budget for a single call, so multi-call MAS gets more effective thinking under the same nominal budget.

our_assessment.why: Visible in the appendix token columns. SAS uses about 1.3k of a 10k budget while Seq uses about 1.8k: 'matched budget' means matched caps, not matched spend. That favours MAS, which strengthens the 'matches' result.

open_questions: How were the bootstrap CIs computed (over questions? over pooled repeated runs?), and how many runs per cell?
How many MuSiQue 4-hop questions were used? We assumed the 405 of the answerable dev set.
Does the SAS >= MAS result hold for long-horizon tasks with artifacts, the regime MASS and RHI target, where the paper's own theory predicts it may not?
